filename: Assessing improvements in global ocean pCO2 machine learning reconstructions with Southern Ocean autonomous sampling(1).pdf
title: Assessing improvements in global ocean pCO2 machine learning reconstructions with Southern Ocean autonomous sampling
testbed_rationale: This study uses an ocean biogeochemistry OSSE / testbed to evaluate mapping and gap-filling algorithms for surface ocean pCO2 rather than generating high-resolution process data for subgrid parameterization.
pain_points: Severe data sparsity in the Southern Ocean (particularly during winter) leading to reconstruction biases and artificial decadal variability
Model overfitting indicated by differences between training and test set error statistics when reconstructing unseen regions
extraction_notes: The paper uses the pCO2-Residual approach with XGBoost on synthetic sampling masks taken from an Earth System Model large ensemble test bed (LET). It focuses on observational network design rather than physical parameterization.
